simple.meaning: שָׂרָה (sârâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a mistress , i.e. female noble.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שָׂרָה (H8282) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 5:29, with occurrences in Judges, 1 Kings, Esther, Isaiah, Lamentations.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׂרָה (H8282) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שָׂרָה (H8282) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שָׂרָה (sârâh) / H8282 is traced through Judges 5:29, 1 Kings 11:3, Esther 1:18, Isaiah 49:23 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H8282. sarah I. [ שָׂרָה ] noun feminine princess, noble lady ; — construct שָׂרָ֫תִי (Ges § 90l ) Lam 1:1 ; plural שָׂרוֺת 1Kin 11:3 , construct id. Est 1:18 ; suffix שָׂרוֺתֶיהָ Judg 5:29 , תֵיהֶם - Isa 49:23 ; — princess attending Sisera's mother Judg 5:29 ; so Solomon's wives 1Kin 11:3 , other queens Isa 49:23 (|| מְלָכִים ); wives of nobles Est 1:18 ; figurative of Jerusalem Lam 1:1 .

occurrences.englishText: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines. His wives turned his heart away.
Today, the princesses of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen’s deed will tell all the king’s princes. This will cause much contempt and wrath.
